item.title: De'Aaron Fox's Surprising New Role With the Spurs: What It Means for San Antonio
item.description:
When a franchise point guard who averaged over 25 points per game for multiple seasons suddenly finds himself in a secondary offensive role, it raises eyebrows across the league. That’s exactly what’s happening with De’Aaron Fox on the San Antonio Spurs — and surprisingly, it might be working.

Key Takeaways

  • Fox is averaging 17.9 points per game since the beginning of March 2026, adjusting to a complementary role alongside Victor Wembanyama
  • He has been named a finalist for an NBA award honoring high character and leadership
  • The Fox-LaVine trade’s impact on both the Spurs and Sacramento Kings is still being debated
  • Despite a rough outing against Chicago (7 points on 3-8 shooting), the Spurs are surging heading into the final stretch

De’Aaron Fox and the Spurs’ Winning Formula

The San Antonio Spurs have been on a tear, and the arrival of De’Aaron Fox has been a significant part of the equation — even if his stat line doesn’t always scream superstar.

item.title: Scottie Barnes: The Essential Force Behind Toronto's Playoff Push
item.description:
What makes a player the backbone of an entire franchise? For the Toronto Raptors, the answer stands 6-foot-8 and weighs nearly 240 pounds. Scottie Barnes isn’t just playing basketball — he’s redefining what it means to be a two-way cornerstone in today’s NBA.

Key Takeaways

  • Barnes is averaging 15.8 points, 5.5 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.4 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game since the start of March 2026
  • The Raptors sit at 38-29, holding the sixth seed in the Eastern Conference by a half-game margin
  • His versatile stat-stuffing ability makes him one of the most physically gifted players in the league
  • Toronto’s defensive identity starts and ends with Barnes

Scottie Barnes and the Raptors’ Defensive Identity

If you’ve watched the Raptors play recently, you’ve noticed something distinct about how they start games. Toronto has made it their business to disrupt opponents’ scripted opening sets with ferocious defensive intensity — and Barnes is the engine driving that approach.

item.title: Cade Cunningham Injury Update: What His Absence Means for the Surging Pistons
item.description:
Cade Cunningham will not suit up Tuesday night against the Washington Wizards, and for a Detroit Pistons franchise riding the highest wave in over a decade, the timing raises real questions about whether their MVP candidate can stay healthy through the postseason push.

Key Takeaway:

  • Cade Cunningham is out Tuesday vs. the Wizards due to an ongoing hip injury
  • He has already missed 3 games this season, also dealing with a left quadriceps issue
  • The Pistons are 13-2 and first in the Eastern Conference, holding a three-game lead over the Cleveland Cavaliers
  • Detroit rode an 11-game winning streak to the top of the standings
  • Cunningham is averaging a career-best 27.3 points per game with 9.9 assists (second in the NBA)
  • At just 24 years old, he recently signed a signature shoe deal with Nike — one of only 6 active NBA players with that distinction

The Rise Nobody Predicted

Two years ago, the Detroit Pistons were the laughingstock of the NBA. Endless losing, revolving-door coaching, and a fanbase that had largely checked out. The idea that Cade Cunningham — the former number one overall pick — would be leading this franchise to first place in the Eastern Conference felt like pure fantasy.
